prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical discovery of time-reversal-invariant topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect, and for their first experimental realisation in HgTe quantum wells

statement.case_for: I opened with the IceCube case (B043) because a new window on the universe is a discovery in the most literal sense, but the opening ballots show that B004 is the candidate on which the committee's judgements converge: seven of eight members place it in their top three, and two put it first. Having reread the arguments, I find the scientific case compelling. Kane and Mele introduced a new organising principle, the Z2 invariant for time-reversal-invariant insulators, in which symmetry and band topology protect edge and surface states without any magnetic field. It was a sharp prediction, it was confirmed in HgTe quantum wells by Molenkamp's group, it generalised to three dimensions, and it has been verified by transport and ARPES in many materials. That is the pattern I look for: a clear idea, tested against nature, with lasting reach across condensed matter and into photonic and superconducting analogues. The theory-plus-experiment structure gives a coherent three-person citation, and fifteen to twenty years of independent confirmation means interpretation is stable.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is attribution. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang made the HgTe proposal that Molenkamp's experiment tested, and Shoucheng Zhang is deceased, so a Kane-Mele-Molenkamp prize leaves out a contributor whose role was arguably decisive for the experimental realisation, and the credit around the 3D generalisation (Fu, Kane, Mele, Moore, Balents) is also not covered. A second concern is overlap with the 2016 prize on topological phase transitions and phases of matter; a committee could reasonably say that topology in condensed matter has already been honoured. I weigh this as a real but not disqualifying objection, because the Z2 class and the quantum spin Hall effect are a distinct conceptual step, but I do not dismiss it.

responses.point: Mehlig ranks B009 first and B004 second, arguing that the Z2 classification extends the topological idea of the 2016 prize into a new symmetry class and a broad programme, while the Bistritzer-MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero pair is a clean theory-experiment match.
responses.response: I agree that B009 is a clean pairing and that a continuum-model prediction followed by experimental discovery is attractive. Where I differ is on maturity: the superconducting mechanism in magic-angle graphene is still debated and the field is moving quickly, whereas the interpretation of B004 has been stable for well over a decade. I also take your point that the 2016 overlap matters, but I read the Z2 class as a new organising principle rather than a continuation, so I keep B004 ahead of B009 while accepting that B009 may well come soon after.

responses.point: Pearce ranks the Higgs observation (B002) first and my own B043 second, on the grounds that the instruments and measurement behind the Higgs remain unrecognised after the 2013 theory prize, and that IceCube opened a new messenger channel.
responses.response: I share your respect for IceCube, which is why it was my first choice, and I note that you and I are the only members to rank it so high. But I have to be honest that the opening ballots do not support B043 as a consensus choice: only four members ranked it, and source identification beyond TXS 0506+056 is still maturing. On the Higgs, the founder-credit problem across ATLAS and CMS, with four proposed names for a three-person limit, is exactly the kind of attribution difficulty that I think makes a prize hard to defend this year. I keep B043 as my first alternative.

responses.point: Eriksson ranks B004 first, arguing that the Z2 insight and its HgTe realisation reshaped how band structures are computed and searched, with fifteen to twenty years of independent confirmation and a defensible theory-plus-experiment triple.
responses.response: I agree with the maturity argument and with the point about electronic-structure practice, which I cannot judge as well as you can. I would qualify only your description of the triple as merely defensible: the omission of Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang is the genuine weakness, and we should be explicit about it in the citation language and not pretend the allocation is uncontroversial. If the committee wants to stay with B004, the citation should be anchored on the Z2 theory and the first experimental observation.

responses.point: Kroll ranks the optical lattice clock (B006) first as a clear, original and lasting advance, and places B004 only third.
responses.response: B006 is a serious candidate and I ranked it fourth. It is clean in attribution, with Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and Ye's drive to 10^-18, and it is mature. My hesitation is the proximity to the earlier prizes for frequency combs and for ion-based optical control, which may make it read as an incremental step in a prize lineage, while B004 is a new organising principle. I would not oppose B006 as a configuration, and I would find it easier to defend on attribution than B004.

uncertainties: How much weight the committee should give to the 2016 topological-matter prize when judging B004, and whether the quantum spin Hall effect is seen as a distinct conceptual step.
Whether leaving out Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang can be defended, given that Zhang is deceased and the credited set is limited to three living names.
Whether the IceCube source-identification evidence will mature enough to make B043 a stronger candidate in a coming year.
I cannot independently verify the priority claims around the 3D generalisation and the first ARPES observations from the supplied text.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile for B004: my documented connections are to David Gross, Hector Rubinstein, Thomas Van Riet and the Uppsala theory group, none of whom is a credited candidate here. My subject-matter background in string theory and cosmology is relevant to B049 and B022, which are not in my preferred configuration.
